question.leadin: Name the following World War II battles in the Pacific.
question.text: Six months after Pearl Harbor, the U.S. sunk four of Japan's aircraft carriers during this battle, named after the atoll where it took place. The USS Yorktown was sunk during this battle.
question.clue: The illness of William Halsey forced Raymond Spruance to take on an unfamiliar command role in this battle, which saw SBD Dauntless Dive Bombers from the Hornet help sink the Mikuma.

swap.leadin: This nation is split into North and South Islands.
swap.text: Name this Pacific island nation with capital Wellington.
swap.clue: This country successfully prosecuted two French citizens for the bombing of the Greenpeace flagship Rainbow Warrior, which was bombed in the harbor of its largest city.

question.text: The silver fern is also a common motif in the art of these indigenous New Zealanders. These peoples signed the Treaty of Waitangi for peace with the British, and are often compared to Australian Aborigines.
question.clue: Tribes of this people experienced bitter infighting in the Musket Wars.

swap.text: This territory's inhabitants are descended from the mutineers on the HMS Bounty, and it is one of the UK's smallest overseas possessions.
swap.clue: Police officer Gail Cox denounced the culture of sexual abuse on this island, the subject of a controversial 2004 trial that convicted six of its residents.

question.text: This man was the President of Hawaii while it was an independent, non-monarchical nation, in addition to owning a fruit company.
question.clue: Lorrin Thurston and John Stevens conspired with this businessman to overthrow Queen Liliuokalani. He was the only president of the Republic of Hawaii.

swap.text: In 1795, Kamehameha [kuh-MAY-hah-MAY-ah] unified the islands of this Kingdom later annexed by the United States. Its Queen Lili'uokalani was overthrown by a committee led by Lorrin Thurston.
swap.clue: Because William C. Lunalilo did not name an heir, supporters of Queen Emma in this nation revolted when David Kalakaua was elected king.

question.leadin: Relocating to Australia has been rather popular throughout history, albeit for different reasons. Answer some questions about humans moving to Australia.
question.text: Islanders from this body of water between New Guinea and Australia may have migrated across it to reach Australia. This body of water is also known as Zenadh Kes.
question.clue: This strait, named for a Spanish explorer, is home to namesake islands populated by indigenous Melanesian people and located between the Cape York Peninsula and the island of New Guinea.

swap.leadin: The Catamaran likely originated from these people.
swap.text: Name these ancient ancestors of people from New Zealand, New Guinea, and Madagascar. Their namesake expansion likely began around 1500-1000BCE.

question.leadin: Answer the following about interactions between early European explorers and the Maori: (MAO-ree).
question.text: This British explorer made contact with the Maori in 1769. This explorer reached locations including Hawai'i and Australia, and lends their name to the strait separating the islands of New Zealand.
question.clue: This figure, although not trained as a scientist, nevertheless received the Royal Society's Copley Medal for techniques that he developed to prevent his crew from contracting scurvy on lengthy Pacific voyages.

swap.leadin: This treaty was the subject of R v. Symonds and another case brought by political leader Wi Parata.
swap.text: Identify this treaty partially crafted by James Freeman and William Hobson and subject to several objections by the local rangatira and cannibalism enthusiast, Moka Kainga-mataa.
swap.clue: The Native Land Act of 1862 struck down the land-selling article, which had been the cause of the Wairau incident led by Te Rauparaha.

question.leadin: Archaeological sites in this ocean include Kilu Cave, "Chief Roi Mata's Domain," and the Taputapuatea marae ("tah-POO-tah-POO-AH-tay-ah mah-RAI").
question.text: Name this ocean where many islands contain dentate-stamped pottery left by the ancient Lapita ("lah-PEE-tah") culture, whose Polynesian descendants spread "canoe plants" like breadfruit and taro.
question.clue: A war named for this body of water included clashes over Tacna and Arica and was partly ended by the Treaty of Ancon (an-KOHN).

swap.leadin: Tensions raised by the execution of Wiremu Maketu helped lead to this war.
swap.text: A gift to James Busby sometimes names what war, during which the H.M.S. Hazard bombarded Kororareka?
swap.clue: This 1845 war, often nicknamed for the object that chief Hone Heke cut down four times at the beginning of hostilities.

question.leadin: Robert Louis Stevenson's book A Footnote to History describes how a diplomatic standoff in this country was averted when a cyclone wrecked all the warships in its harbor.
question.text: Name this modern-day country whose independence was advocated for by the Mau movement. Germany was granted administration of this island country in 1899, while the US administered a set of islands to the east.
question.clue: This country's independence was demanded on "Black Saturday" by the Olaf Frderick Nelson-led Mau Movement.

swap.leadin: This country's Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka was nicknamed "Colonel Steve Rambo" after his tendency to quote the Sylvester Stallone movie Rambo to describe a 1987 coup against Timoci Bavadra.
swap.text: Name this country whose first indigenous prime minister Kamisese Mara attempted to seize power from Mahendra Chaudhry, who descended from the girmityas, during a coup led by George Speight in 2000.
swap.answerHtml: Fiji [or Republic of Fiji; or Matanitu Tugalala o Viti]
swap.clue: After removing Laisenia Qarase (un-guh-RAH-seh) from power, Frank Bainimarama became this country's prime minister.

question.leadin: Unmixed examples of these people went extinct after the death of Tommy Solomon in 1933.
question.text: Name this group of people whose genocide was enabled by the philosophy of nonviolence known as Nunuku's Law. These original inhabitants of the Chatham ("CHAT-um") Islands were massacred during the Musket Wars.
question.clue: These people are inaccurately depicted laboring on American-style plantations in the first chapter of (+) Cloud Atlas.

swap.leadin: This ruler won a battle that was so violent that it became known as the "damming of the waters" due to the corpses blocking the flow of the 'Iao ("EE-ow").
swap.text: Name ruler who won a decisive victory at Kepaniwai with the help of Welsh cannoneer Isaac Davis. This ruler hired Australian convicts Mela and Black Jack to design the Brick Palace for his favorite queen, Ka'ahumanu ("kuh-AH-hoo-MAH-noo").
swap.clue: This ruler who established the Law of the Splintered Paddle after winning battles at Kawela and the Pali Lookout.

question.leadin: This battle resulted in over 500 Japanese aircraft destroyed.
question.text: Name this 1944 naval battle in the namesake body of water which occurred as the United States began its "island-hopping" campaign at Saipan. It was known as the "Great Marianas Turkey Shoot" for the large number of Japanese losses.
question.clue: Submarines sank the Shokaku and Taiho in this battle, allowing Mark Mitscher to order a counterattack.

swap.text: One of Vogel's first projects was completing the Main South Line, which passed through this region that he had been governor of. In the 1860s, a major gold rush began near Gabriel's Gully in this region.

question.leadin: Native speakers of this language started to use the word palapala in the 1820s to refer to the body of written knowledge produced with the help of Christian missionaries.
question.text: Name this language. The nineteenth-century historians Davida Malo and "Kepelino" both wrote in this language, and Lorrin A. Thurston wrote a constitution in this language.

swap.text: In spite of being ostensibly committed to socialism as a member of the Labour Party, this finance minister implemented a series of supply-side reforms in the 1980s to try to restart New Zealand's stagnant economy.
